MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which expression shows "the sum of a and 9"? (1 mark)
   A. a ÷ 9
   B. a + 9
   C. 9a
   D. a − 9

2. Simplify 2c + 3d + 4c. (1 mark)
   A. 9cd
   B. 6c + 7d
   C. 2c + 7d
   D. 6c + 3d

3. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1. (1 mark)
   A. 5a + 5
   B. 6a + 5
   C. 11a
   D. 5a + 6

4. Change 400 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 4 m
   B. 4 m 50 cm
   C. 5 m
   D. 40 cm

5. A rectangle is 15 cm long and 10 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 150 cm
   B. 52 cm
   C. 25 cm
   D. 50 cm

6. A square has sides of 15 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 45 m
   B. 60 m
   C. 30 m
   D. 225 m

7. A rectangle has an area of 60 square units and 5 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 13
   C. 65
   D. 55

8. A rectangle has an area of 45 square units and 9 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 54
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 36

9. A rectangle has 5 rows and 8 columns. How many small squares are needed to cover it? (1 mark)
   A. 45
   B. 40
   C. 26
   D. 13

10. What does volume measure? (1 mark)
   A. The time an event takes
   B. The space a solid object takes up
   C. The distance round a shape
   D. The flat surface a shape covers

11. How many small cubes make a big cube that is 2 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks high? (1 mark)
   A. 16
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 4

12. A cuboid is 10 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 17 blocks
   B. 50 blocks
   C. 100 blocks
   D. 110 blocks

13. What is 2 L + 1 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2 L
   B. 3 3/4 L
   C. 3 1/4 L
   D. 4 L

14. Two quarters of a litre are the same as (1 mark)
   A. 1 L
   B. 3/4 L
   C. 1/4 L
   D. 1/2 L

15. What is 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/4 kg
   B. 4 1/2 kg
   C. 5 kg
   D. 4 3/4 kg

16. A goat has a mass of 32 kg and a sheep 27 kg. How much heavier is the goat? (1 mark)
   A. 5 kg
   B. 59 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 6 kg

17. What is 5 kg − 1 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/4 kg
   D. 4 kg

18. What is 1 h 20 min + 45 min? (1 mark)
   A. 1 h 5 min
   B. 2 h 5 min
   C. 2 h 15 min
   D. 1 h 55 min

19. Lunch is at one o'clock in the afternoon. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 1:00 p.m.
   B. 1:00 a.m.
   C. 1:00 noon
   D. 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 a.m.

20. How many minutes does the minute hand take to go once round the clock face? (1 mark)
   A. 12 minutes
   B. 24 minutes
   C. 30 minutes
   D. 60 minutes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each and 2 packets of 1 L each. How many litres of milk is that altogether? (3 marks)

22. Work out 4 L − 1 3/4 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

23. School starts at 8:00 a.m. and ends at 3:15 p.m. Lunch is from 12:40 p.m. to 1:40 p.m. (a) How long is the school day? (b) How long is it from the start of school to the start of lunch? (c) How long is it from the end of lunch to the end of school? (5 marks)

24. Work out 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L. (3 marks)

25. Find the area of a square with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. Then find the area of a rectangle with 5 rows of 7 squares. Which is bigger? (4 marks)

26. A stack of soda crates has 5 crates along the wall, 4 crates deep and 4 layers high. How many crates are in the stack? (3 marks)

27. Add 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

28. A rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. Peter walks once round the plot. How far does he walk? (3 marks)

29. A trip leaves at 7:45 a.m. and takes 2 hours 30 minutes. At what time does it arrive? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — a + 9
   The key words tell us the operation. "the sum of a and 9" is written a + 9.

2. D — 6c + 3d
   Only like terms can be joined. 2c + 3d + 4c = 6c + 3d.

3. D — 5a + 6
   Only like terms can be joined. 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 = 5a + 6.

4. A — 4 m
   400 ÷ 100 = 4 remainder 0. So 400 cm = 4 m.

5. D — 50 cm
   Perimeter = 15 + 10 + 15 + 10 = 50 cm.

6. B — 60 m
   A square has four equal sides. 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60.

7. A — 12
   Rows × columns = 60, so columns = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

8. B — 5
   Rows × columns = 45, so columns = 45 ÷ 9 = 5.

9. B — 40
   5 × 8 = 40 squares.

10. B — The space a solid object takes up
   Volume is the amount of space that a solid fills.

11. B — 8
   2 × 2 = 4 in a layer and 4 × 2 = 8 blocks.

12. C — 100 blocks
   One layer has 10 × 5 = 50 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 50 × 2 = 100 blocks.

13. A — 3 1/2 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 2 L + 1 1/2 L = 3 1/2 L.

14. D — 1/2 L
   1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

15. D — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 3 1/2 kg + 1 1/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

16. A — 5 kg
   32 − 27 = 5 kg.

17. B — 3 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 5 kg − 1 1/2 kg = 3 1/2 kg.

18. B — 2 h 5 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 2 h 5 min.

19. A — 1:00 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 1:00 p.m..

20. D — 60 minutes
   The minute hand takes one hour, which is 60 minutes.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 L (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 L (1 mark); total 3 1/2 L (1 mark).

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 4 L to 3 4/4 L (1 mark). 3 4/4 − 1 3/4 = 2 1/4 (1 mark). Check: 2 1/4 + 1 3/4 = 4 L (1 mark).

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 7 hours 15 minutes (b) 4 hours 40 minutes (c) 1 hour 35 minutes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 7 hours and then 15 minutes (2 marks); (b) 8:00 to 12:40 is 4 h 40 min (1 mark); (c) 1:40 p.m. to 3:15 p.m. is 1 h 35 min (2 marks).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); answer 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Square 36, rectangle 35. The square is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each area and 1 mark for the comparison and 1 mark for the difference.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 80 crates
   Working / marking points: 5 × 4 = 20 per layer (1 mark); 20 × 4 (1 mark); 80 crates (1 mark).

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 m 25 cm
   Working / marking points: 345 + 280 = 625 cm (2 marks); 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm (1 mark).

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 40 m
   Working / marking points: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. 1 mark for identifying perimeter, 1 mark for the sum, 1 mark for unit.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10:15 a.m.
   Working / marking points: 7:45 + 2 h = 9:45 (1 mark); 9:45 + 30 min = 10:15 (1 mark); a.m. stated (1 mark).
